source.title: Learning Overparameterized Neural Networks via Stochastic Gradient Descent on Structured Data

record.tranche_reason: Theoretical analysis and synthetic/MNIST experiments bear on fitting arbitrary labels and generalization, but the experiments do not reproduce the original random-label intervention.
record.gate_note: The authors state that their theorem implies SGD can fit arbitrary labels when each input is treated as its own component. This is a theoretical implication under the paper's data-separation and overparameterization assumptions, not an experiment with randomized labels. The true-label experiments report test accuracy and are recorded separately. Cited findings about random-label memorization are not rows.
record.test_reason: Section 4 derives arbitrary-label fitting by SGD as an implication of the authors' theorem for sufficiently wide two-layer ReLU networks on separated inputs. This bears on V1 theoretically; the experiments use true labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate with qualifications: the authors prove small population classification error for SGD on sufficiently overparameterized two-layer ReLU networks under separated-component assumptions, and derive arbitrary-label fitting by treating individual inputs as components. They do not experimentally demonstrate random-label fitting.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies a two-layer overparameterized ReLU network with fixed top-layer weights and SGD under explicit separated-component data assumptions; it does not run the original random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that test accuracy decreases and takes longer to improve as synthetic component variance or the number of components per class increases; the trends for activation patterns, distance, and update rank remain similar.

fits_no_version.finding: True-label synthetic test accuracy quickly reaches 100%; MNIST experiments show qualitatively similar trends.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD can generalize on structured data using sufficiently overparameterized two-layer ReLU networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing synthetic component variance or the number of components per class lowers test accuracy and delays improvement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning and generalization depend on input-distribution structure; these interventions do not measure label-corruption effects.

record.problems: The arbitrary-label fitting statement is a theoretical implication under restrictive separation and overparameterization assumptions, not a direct random-label experiment. The paper does not report chance test error for arbitrary labels. Experiment plots summarize five repetitions with mean and standard deviation, but the text provides few numerical values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results on random labels, corrupted labels, unstructured inputs, regularization, or learning order are reported. Figure-only quantities such as activation-pattern difference and distance do not measure a version's named behavior and were omitted.

untested.parts: Empirical fitting by standard deep architectures; chance test error under completely random labeling; unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters relative to true-label training.
Training-time ratio for random versus true labels and convergence as the fraction of corrupted labels increases.
Training-set fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across label-corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and of their removal on true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy labels; comparative learning trajectories for real and random labels.

record.verdict_notes: The theoretical assumptions delimit the support; they do not demonstrate failure outside those assumptions. True-label generalization and polynomial convergence bounds do not establish V2's random-versus-real training-time comparison or V6's learning order.

versions.untested_parts: No empirical random-label experiment; test error at chance and unchanged architecture or hyperparameters relative to a true-label run are not tested.
